 By TED CORDERO , GMA News Published October 21, 2026 5:16pm 
 + Add GMA on Google Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google. Manila Water Company Inc. said Tuesday it is keeping its non-revenue water (NRW) or system loss below 15% as it strengthens its preparations for the anticipated impacts of a looming strong El Niño.
 In a news release, Manila Water said it recorded an NRW level of 14.65% as of August, bringing the year-to-date level at 14.29%.
 A 1% reduction in NRW translates to an additional 15 million to 16 million liters delivered to customers, according to the water distribution utility.
 The NRW refers to treated water that is produced but does not get billed as water is lost due to leaks, pipe bursts, illegal connections, tampered meters, and other commercial losses.

 Manila Water said keeping NRW at low levels allows more water to be delivered to customers without drawing additional supplies from existing water sources.
The company said the sustained NRW performance reflects nearly three decades of investments in leak detection and repair, mainline extension and rehabilitation, district metering, meter replacement, pressure management, network monitoring, and preventive maintenance. 
 From an NRW level of about 63% at the start of its concession in 1997, Manila Water said it has steadily reduced system losses to below 15%.
 "Keeping system losses low is one of the most effective ways to stretch available water resources, especially as we prepare for the challenges posed by climate change and extreme weather events such as El Niño. Every drop recovered from our network is a drop that can be delivered to our customers," said Dittie Galang, Manila Water Communication Affairs Department head.
Manila Water said it continues to diversify its water sources and strengthen its network infrastructure, maintaining world-class NRW performance remains a key pillar of the company's strategy to ensure water security and reliable 24/7 service for its more than 7.9 million customers, particularly during periods of prolonged dry weather. — VDV, GMA News
